title: Arctic-SWE: Revisiting the Long Horizon Agent Training by Modeling-System Co-Design
data_curation: Two-pipeline curation over 21,099 existing tasks (R2E-Gym 3,606, SWE-rebench V2 6,584, Scale-SWE 10,909); no new tasks are synthesized. Pipeline 1 (execution only) re-runs suites on buggy and gold trees and instruments binding assertions, keeping 17,861 (84.7%). Pipeline 2 gives a Qwen3.8-27B agent the gold patch, tests and a shell, and asks in fixed order whether gold fixes the issue, whether tests grade the issue (settled by writing plausible-but-wrong and correct-but-different counterfactual patches scored with the RL scorer), and whether the issue states what tests demand; it keeps 7,500 (6,267 unchanged, 1,233 issues rewritten). 5,351 suites (30%) are too_loose; test strengthening repairs 4,909 (91.7%). Git history is pruned and egress denied in all sandboxes; decks are screened against SWE-bench Verified at ID and repository level.
curriculum: No SFT stage: RL starts directly from Qwen3.5-4B/9B. The recipe is first stress-tested by prolonged overfitting on 160 solvable R2E-Gym tasks (32 tasks x 5 rollouts), then trained on 3,606 unchanged R2E-Gym tasks for 800 updates, then on the 7,500-row curated deck (the reported 9B run uses 12,389 rows including strengthened suites). Tasks are drawn without replacement from one global shuffled deck; easy eviction retires a task once a group solves it 8/8, and (in the R2E-Gym run) hard eviction retires it after three consecutive 0/8 groups. AdamW at constant LR 1e-6, beta2 0.98, no warmup or decay.
method: Fully asynchronous RL on Prime-RL (8x B200: 2 trainer GPUs, 6 vLLM engines) with the Mini-SWE-Agent-Plus harness (execute_bash, edit_via_str_replace; 100 turns, 131,072 tokens). Loss: CISPO with detached importance weight, token-mean over the batch, group-centered advantage without std normalization, no reference KL, entropy bonus or length penalty; IcePop-style masking of tokens with ratio >2 (two-sided [0.5,2.0] for the reported 9B); zero-advantage groups filtered. Feedback fixes: gated reward (explicit exact submission required; format errors, duplicate calls and exhausted budgets end the rollout) plus a raw-token format check that rejects all 13 malformed Qwen3.5 turns that public stacks partly execute; invalid trajectories get -1 in Section 5. System fixes: FP32 GatedDeltaNet recurrent state, gate arithmetic and A_log through training and weight transfer; full KV/recurrent-cache recomputation after each weight refresh; load-aware per-rank dispatch capping resident sequences; off-policy cap 8 updates.
eval_metrics: pass@1 as average over 4 rollouts on a fixed 483-problem SWE-bench Verified subset (17 excluded as ungradeable offline) and all 731 SWE-bench Pro problems (Pro-v1, Pro-v2, Pro-v2 Python subset), evaluated at T=1.0, top-p 0.95 in isolated sandboxes. Diagnostics: training reward, token entropy, rollout-trainer mismatch KL, stale drops, policy lag. Overfit test: full recipe reaches 93.0% (epochs 100-150) and 95.8% (200-230) where Prime-RL and SkyRL recipes collapse after ~70%. Ablations on Verified: std-normalized advantages -1.7, per-rollout aggregation -3.4, length penalties collapse to 20.3%/8.4%. Auditing finds unsealed sandboxes let Qwen3.8-27B hack 19/60 Pro trials (50.0% to 65.0%).
key_results: On unchanged R2E-Gym data, Arctic-SWE lifts Qwen3.5-4B from 47.4% to 62.0% SWE-bench Verified pass@1, matching FrogNano's 61.5% with about one-sixth the training rollouts. With curated data the 4B reaches 65.0/38.3/59.7 and the 9B 65.7/39.6/70.2 on Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2 (from 47.4/25.0/37.9 and 56.2/31.9/48.8).
evolution_note: Arctic-SWE reacts to SWE-agent RL works (R2E-Gym, DeepSWE, SkyRL, FrogNano, MiMo) whose baselines are hard to reproduce, arguing many reported gains may be measured against under-tuned recipes. It assembles known pieces (CISPO, IcePop masking, PipelineRL-style async with KV recomputation, gated rewards) into a reproducible async baseline validated by an RL-overfitting stress test, and shows fail-to-pass validation is too weak, motivating counterfactual-patch auditing and test strengthening of training rewards. It also documents git-history and network reward hacking and forgetting of evicted tasks in small models as open problems for agent RL.
